# GENERATION_NOTES.md — Global Dataset Documentation

> Spec §7.3. One-time, not per-mine. Records every unit, every parameter
> **range** the generator samples from, and every modeling choice — so the
> dataset can be understood without reading the code.

**Generated by:** `minegen/` · **Schema version:** 2.0.0
**Authoritative sources:** tier/sensor image (hardware) · `mesh-communication-mechanics.md` (network) · `mine_collapse_data_spec.md` v2.0 (objective, labels, output)

---

## 1. Units

| Quantity | Unit |
|---|---|
| Distance / position | metres (m) |
| Subsidence | metres, **down-positive** |
| Tilt / inclination | microradians (µrad) |
| Acceleration | g (1 g = 9.80665 m/s²) |
| Angular rate | degrees/second (deg/s) |
| Strain | microstrain (µε) |
| Fissure opening | millimetres (mm) |
| Extensometer delta | millimetres (mm) |
| Pore pressure | kilopascals (kPa) |
| Soil moisture | % volumetric water content |
| Temperature | degrees Celsius (°C) |
| Vibration rms/peak | mm/s |
| Dominant frequency | hertz (Hz) |
| Time | seconds since that mine's t0 |
| Time-to-collapse | seconds (NaN when censored) |

---

## 2. Parameter ranges

Every value below is drawn **per mine** and written into that mine's `metadata.json`.

### 2.1 Cadence and horizon

| Parameter | Range |
|---|---|
| Sampling interval | **60 s** (fixed — the TDMA superframe) |
| Simulated horizon | 2–14 days |
| Timesteps per mine | 2,880–20,160 |

### 2.2 Geometry

| Parameter | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Mine extent X | 400–1200 m | full site width |
| Mine extent Y | 200–1000 m | full site height |
| Panel width frac | 0.45–0.75 | extracted panel vs extent |
| Panel height frac | 0.35–0.65 | extracted panel vs extent |
| Depth `H` | 60–300 m | depth of workings |
| Seam thickness | 1.5–6.0 m | extracted seam |
| `tan_beta` | 1.6–2.6 | angle of draw; r = H/tan_beta |
| Subsidence factor `a` | 0.45–0.85 | S_max = a × seam |
| `B_frac` | 0.28–0.38 | B = B_frac × r, horiz. displacement |
| Knothe `c` | 0.05–0.60 /day | time-function rate |

### 2.3 Node placement (geotechnical, per `mesh-communication-mechanics.md` §2)

| Parameter | Range |
|---|---|
| Scout spacing (1A/1B/1C) | 15–25 m |
| Anchor spacing (2A/2B) | 100–150 m |
| Gateway standoff (3) | 500–1000 m beyond panel + r |
| Scout count | 18–70, then **capped by anchor capacity** (see below) |
| Tier 2A count | **derived**: `max(3, ceil(n_scouts/5) - n_2B)` |
| Tier 2B count | 1–3 (independent — sited for geology, not radio) |
| Gateway count | 1 (fixed) |
| Scout tier mix | Dirichlet around 1A 0.45 / 1B 0.35 / 1C 0.20 |
| Borehole depths | 5 m, 15 m, 30 m, 50 m (fixed) |

**Anchor counts are derived, not drawn.** One Anchor parents at most 6 Scouts
(§7.3 below), so anchors must be numerous enough to adopt every scout placed:
`n_anchors_needed = ceil(n_scouts / 5)`. Drawing the two independently — as an
earlier version did — produced up to 13.8 scouts per anchor, describing a
network that cannot physically exist.

**Scouts are then capped by real anchor capacity.** Anchors need 100–150 m
separation, so a small monitoring rectangle cannot host many (a 340×160 m site
at 139 m spacing fits ~3). Dart-throwing packs at ~0.87 of ideal square packing:
```
max_anchors = max(2, int(0.87 * rect_area / anchor_spacing**2))
n_scouts    = min(n_scouts, max_anchors * 5)
```
Smaller mines therefore carry fewer scouts, which is the physically honest
outcome. Measured over the 100-mine batch: **mean cluster size 4.80, max 6,
zero breaches.**

**Placement method:** dart-throwing (Poisson-disc) with a minimum-separation
constraint, biased per tier toward the zone that tier watches. Deliberately
**not** a jittered grid — a jittered grid retains grid structure at long range,
which spec §3.3 forbids.

| Tier | Placement bias |
|---|---|
| 1A | flat interior of the subsidence bowl |
| 1B | high-curvature panel edges (shear zones) |
| 1C | a per-mine fault/water corridor at a random angle |
| 2A | spread across the monitoring rectangle |
| 2B | over the panel, sparse |
| 3 | outside the angle of draw, on bedrock |

### 2.4 Collapse

| Parameter | Value / range |
|---|---|
| Mines that collapse | **Per-mine draw from Beta(3, 2)**, then flipped — not one fixed rate. Mean 0.60, 10th–90th pct 0.32–0.86, so a 100-mine batch realises ~43–73% collapsing. The drawn probability is recorded in each mine's `metadata.json` as `collapse_probability_drawn`, so any subset's base rate is recoverable. **Why:** real sites differ in how failure-prone they are; a single global rate would bake one base rate into the data and teach the model a prior it should not hold. |
| Events per collapsing mine | 1–3 |
| Precursor window | 0.3–5.0 days, clipped to ≤70% of horizon |
| Severity | 0.15–1.00 (unitless 0–1) |
| Failure threshold | 0.55–0.90 × that mine's peak settled curvature |
| Collapse time | uniform in 45%–97% of horizon |
| Event radius | 0.25–0.75 × r |
| Extra subsidence | severity × 0.15–0.55 × S_max |

## 3. The physics model

### 3.1 One surface, many questions

**Every ground-reading channel is a derivative of one latent subsidence
surface.** They are never generated independently — doing so would make them
trivially consistent and teach a model nothing about the physical coupling
that is the entire point of a multi-sensor network.

```
r        = H / tan_beta                          radius of influence
S_max    = a * seam_thickness                    fully-settled peak
P(x)     = ½[erf(√π(x-x₁)/r) - erf(√π(x-x₂)/r)]  Knothe profile, x-axis
Q(y)     = same form in y
S_final  = S_max · P(x) · Q(y)                   fully-settled bowl
g(t)     = 1 - exp(-c·t)                         Knothe time function, t days

S(x,y,t) = S_final(x,y) · g(t)                   THE MASTER FORMULA
```

Space and time are **separable**: the surface at any instant is one fixed
image times one scalar. That is what makes the dataset generatable at scale.

| Channel | Derived as |
|---|---|
| `tilt_x`, `tilt_y` | ∂S/∂x, ∂S/∂y — first derivative |
| `strain_ue` | B · ∂²S/∂y² — second derivative |
| `fissure_mm` | horizontal strain integrated over the 0.5 m gauge length |
| `ext_delta_mm` | exact 3-D distance change between two pegs 10 m apart, **including the vertical component** — differential settlement shortens the wire even at zero horizontal strain |
| `accel_{x,y,z}` | gravity vector projected through the local tilt |
| `borehole_tilt_dN` | surface tilt attenuated by exp(−depth/r) |
| `gps_d{x,y,z}` | displacement at the gateway — **zero by construction**, it sits outside the angle of draw |

**Validated:** closed-form derivatives match finite differences to ~1e-6;
separability exact to 1e-16; volume conservation ratio 1.0000.

### 3.2 Collapse events

A collapse is a localised Gaussian subsidence bulb superimposed on the smooth
bowl. It grows through its precursor window on an **accelerating (cubic) ramp**
and saturates after failure. The acceleration is what makes the precursor
detectable: the signal is not merely large near failure, it is *curving upward*.

### 3.3 Channels NOT derived from the surface

The ground cannot explain a passing truck or the weather, so these have their
own independent generators:

| Channel | Model |
|---|---|
| `die_temp_c` | shared air temperature (mean + diurnal sine) + per-node frozen self-heating offset |
| `moisture_pct` | baseline + Poisson rain events with exponential drying, **plus** a precursor rise near a collapse site. Rain is **shared mine-wide** (one sky); the precursor rise is **local** — that contrast is what lets a GNN separate weather from ground. ⚠️ **Least physically-grounded channel**: unlike tilt/strain it is not derived from the subsidence surface, it is asserted |
| `pore_pressure_kpa` | baseline + precursor rise as the failure zone loads up |
| `vib_*` | four independent sources (truck / conveyor / blast / microseismic) |
| `gyro_*` | **no true rotation** — the ground tilts far too slowly to register, so the gyro reports only its own bias walking around |

---

## 4. Vibration model

MPU-6050 burst: **400 Hz × 256 samples**, once per 60 s
superframe, reduced on-node to `vib_rms`, `vib_peak`, `vib_fdom`.

### 4.1 Frequency bands — the whole discriminator in one number

| Source | Band | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Truck | 8.0–20.0 Hz | heavy vehicle — ignore |
| Conveyor | 49.5–50.5 Hz | narrow-band machinery line — notch out |
| Blast | 40.0–80.0 Hz | check the blast register — veto if logged |
| **Microseismic** | 100.0–250.0 Hz | **rock actually cracking — this one counts** |

Microseismic Poisson rate = `0.4/hour × (1 + 25.0·|strain|/1000)`,
so shaking genuinely increases as the ground approaches failure rather than
being painted on afterwards.

> **Observed:** vibration rms rises ~9× near an event before collapse. The
> frequency band confirms *source type*; **amplitude** carries the spatial signal.

---

## 5. Noise model

Spec §4.5 is non-negotiable: no clean signals. Fixed stage order:

```
  1. temp_bias
  2. drift_bias
  3. white_noise
  4. quantise
```

Order matters. Temperature bias is a physical property of the die and exists
before the readout chain adds noise; quantisation is last because it is the ADC
packing an already-corrupted analogue value into an integer.

**This is why `die_temp` is carried on every node** even though the sensor
image does not list it: without the temperature that produced the bias, the
bias is uncorrectable.

### 5.1 Per-channel magnitudes

| Channel | White σ | Bias drift σ/√day | Temp coeff /°C |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mpu_tilt_urad` | 120 | 90 | 14 |
| `adxl_tilt_urad` | 3 | 2.2 | 0.35 |
| `accel_g` | 0.004 | 0.0012 | 0.00015 |
| `gyro_dps` | 0.06 | 0.02 | 0.004 |
| `strain_ue` | 12 | 9 | 1.6 |
| `fissure_mm` | 0.05 | 0.035 | 0.006 |
| `ext_mm` | 0.08 | 0.05 | 0.009 |
| `moisture_pct` | 0.45 | 0.25 | 0.02 |
| `pore_kpa` | 1.2 | 0.8 | 0.05 |
| `borehole_tilt_urad` | 25 | 18 | 2 |
| `vib_mm_s` | 0.02 | 0.008 | 0.0015 |
| `die_temp_c` | 0.15 | 0.05 | 0 |
| `gps_mm` | 2.5 | 1.5 | 0.08 |

Reference temperature: **25.0 °C**. Per-node personality (temperature
coefficient ±25%, white-noise scale 0.75–1.4×) is drawn **once per node and
frozen** — never re-drawn per timestep, so two runs of a seed are identical.

### 5.2 Quantisation (LSB per channel)

| Channel | LSB |
|---|---|
| `tilt_urad` | 2 |
| `accel_g` | 6.10352e-05 |
| `gyro_dps` | 0.00763359 |
| `strain_ue` | 1 |
| `fissure_mm` | 0.01 |
| `ext_mm` | 0.01 |
| `moisture_pct` | 0.1 |
| `pore_kpa` | 0.1 |
| `vib_mm_s` | 0.01 |
| `vib_fdom_hz` | 1 |
| `die_temp_c` | 0.1 |
| `gps_mm` | 0.1 |

### 5.3 The precision gap that justifies Tier 2A

ADXL355 white σ = **3 µrad** vs MPU-6050 **120 µrad**
— a **40× gap**. Reproducing this is what makes Tier 2A
meaningful in the data rather than a duplicate of Tier 1A.

## 6. Labels

Three **separate** columns (spec §5.3: the weight must never be baked into the time value):

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `time_to_collapse_s` | seconds until the **nearest relevant** event. NaN when censored |
| `censored_flag` | 1 = horizon ended with no collapse observed for this node's region |
| `spatial_weight` | how much to trust this node's time label |

**Decay function:** `w = exp(-0.5·(d/σ)²)` with `σ = 1.25 × r`, floored at `0.0001`.

**Relevance rule:** a node is assigned to the nearest event within **4 × the event radius**.
Beyond that the event is treated as not having affected it — so a node can be
**censored even in a mine that collapsed elsewhere**. This is deliberate: a
distant node genuinely did survive the horizon.

**Censored rows carry NaN**, never a sentinel that could pass as a real duration.

---

## 7. Output format

Parquet (zstd), one self-contained folder per mine:

```
/mine_00001/
  metadata.json            every drawn parameter + seed
  nodes.parquet            node_id, tier, node_type, x, y, z
  mesh.parquet             static mesh topology, one row per node
  readings.parquet         long format: one row per node per timestep
  labels.parquet           time_to_collapse_s, censored_flag, spatial_weight
  collapse_events.parquet  mine-level event list
```

**Null vs zero matters.** A channel a tier does not carry is **null**, never
zero-filled. A zero is a measurement; a null is an absence.

### 7.1 Channels by tier

| Tier | Channels |
|---|---|
| **1A** | `tilt_x_urad`, `tilt_y_urad`, `accel_x_g`, `accel_y_g`, `accel_z_g`, `gyro_x_dps`, `gyro_y_dps`, `gyro_z_dps`, `vib_rms_mm_s`, `vib_peak_mm_s`, `vib_fdom_hz`, `die_temp_c` |
| **1B** | `tilt_x_urad`, `tilt_y_urad`, `accel_x_g`, `accel_y_g`, `accel_z_g`, `gyro_x_dps`, `gyro_y_dps`, `gyro_z_dps`, `vib_rms_mm_s`, `vib_peak_mm_s`, `vib_fdom_hz`, `die_temp_c`, `fissure_mm`, `strain_ue` |
| **1C** | `tilt_x_urad`, `tilt_y_urad`, `accel_x_g`, `accel_y_g`, `accel_z_g`, `gyro_x_dps`, `gyro_y_dps`, `gyro_z_dps`, `vib_rms_mm_s`, `vib_peak_mm_s`, `vib_fdom_hz`, `die_temp_c`, `moisture_pct`, `ext_delta_mm` |
| **2A** | `tilt_x_urad`, `tilt_y_urad`, `die_temp_c` |
| **2B** | `pore_pressure_kpa`, `borehole_tilt_d1_urad`, `borehole_tilt_d2_urad`, `borehole_tilt_d3_urad`, `borehole_tilt_d4_urad`, `die_temp_c` |
| **3** | `gps_dx_mm`, `gps_dy_mm`, `gps_dz_mm`, `die_temp_c` |

### 7.3 Mesh topology (`mesh.parquet`) — the 138-byte bundle rule

Columns: `node_id`, `parent_id`, `backup_parent_id`, `cluster_id` (= the head
anchor's `node_id`), `hop_count` (gateway 0 / anchor 1 / scout 2),
`dist_to_parent_m`, `dist_to_backup_m`, `tx_power_dbm_nominal`. The gateway row
carries null parent and backup.

**Fan-out: 5 nominal, 6 hard maximum.** This is arithmetic, not preference.
`mesh-communication-mechanics.md` §3 has an Anchor bundle its children into one
**138-byte** payload; §4 fixes a Scout packet at exactly **23 bytes**:

```
138 / 23 = exactly 6 scout packets per bundle
```

A 7th child needs 161 B and overflows the bundle. Six is a physical ceiling;
five is the design point, leaving one slot of headroom so an orphan failing over
from a dead neighbouring anchor still fits. The TDMA window is *not* the binding
constraint — t=2.0–11.5 s at 250 ms slots is 38 slots, and a Scout needs
90.4 ms TX + 20 ms ACK = 110.4 ms. The payload is what caps it.

**Assignment is capacitated.** Nearest-anchor assignment is unbalanced and would
hand one anchor 9 children. Instead all (scout, anchor) pairs are sorted by
ascending distance and taken greedily, skipping any anchor already at 6; a scout
whose nearest anchor is full falls to its next-nearest. `build_mesh` raises
rather than emitting a network that violates the limit.

**TX power** (mesh doc §3.2): ≤150 m → +5 dBm, ≤500 m → +10 dBm, else +14 dBm.
The +22 dBm maximum is reserved for the emergency blast and is never nominal.

**This is the communication DAG, NOT the GNN edge list.** Spec §6 forbids
shipping edges; they are constructed downstream by kNN/radius. Do not feed
`parent_id` in as adjacency.

### 7.2 Ground-truth companion columns

`readings.parquet` also carries clean, un-corrupted `truth_tilt_x_urad`,
`truth_tilt_y_urad`, `truth_strain_ue`, `truth_subsidence_m` — the quantities the
sensors are noisy proxies for.

> ### ⚠️ Truth columns are DEBUG-ONLY
>
> The model for this dataset is a **Mamba-style SSM + spatiotemporal GNN** doing
> survival analysis (spec §1). There is **no physics loss** anywhere in it.
> Therefore:
>
> - **Never a model input.** Feeding `truth_*` to the SSM or GNN leaks the answer:
>   the model copies it, scores perfectly, and has learned nothing.
> - **Never a training target.** The targets are the three label columns in
>   `labels.parquet`, nothing else.
> - **Their only job is answering "is the data wrong, or is the model wrong?"**
>   With survival labels you cannot eyeball correctness — a hazard curve has no
>   obvious "looks right". These columns let you verify that tilt really is the
>   slope of the surface and that labels line up with the physics, without
>   regenerating the dataset.
>
> They cost ~51% of `readings.parquet` (~13 GB per 1,000 mines). Kept because
> Parquet is columnar: a loader that does not select these columns never reads
> those bytes from disk. **You pay in storage, not in training speed.**
>
> **Loader rule:** select feature columns explicitly. Never `SELECT *`.

---

## 8. Reproducibility

One seed per mine drives every draw. Re-running a seed reproduces the mine
**byte-identically** (verified on `readings`, `labels`, `nodes`, `metadata`).
Per-node personality is frozen at placement, never re-drawn per timestep.

---

## 9. Known gaps — deliberate, not oversights

| Gap | Status |
|---|---|
| **Mesh packet loss** | **Not simulated.** Every node reports perfectly every 60 s, so `readings.parquet` is a dense `n_nodes × n_steps` rectangle. `mesh-communication-mechanics.md` describes ACKs, dead anchors and backup routing; deferred by decision to keep the dataset simple. Recorded in each mine's `metadata.json` under `deferred`. Note the *static* topology (who parents whom, and each node's pre-calculated backup) **is** modelled — see `mesh.parquet` and §7.3. |
| **Node death at collapse** | **Not simulated.** Nodes report straight through a collapse rather than being destroyed or orphaned. Consequence, stated plainly: the sensor nearest a collapse keeps emitting clean data through the event, whereas in reality its sudden silence would be one of the strongest precursor signals available. Acceptable for a first training run; the highest-value realism upgrade available later. Design for adding it is in `MESH_UPGRADE_BRIEF.md` §7. |
| **Geophone** | Removed — no geophone in the final hardware. Replaced by the MPU-6050 vibration burst. |
| **Battery / solar** | Present on every row of the sensor image, but describes hardware, not ground. Not emitted. |
| **Strain not clipped** | Peak magnitudes reach ~20,000 µε in severe collapses. Left unclipped: it is within a real foil gauge's ±32,767 range, and clipping would flatten the largest-signal cases the model most needs. |
| **Vibration band does not localise** | Microseismic share is ~72% both near and far from an event. This is realistic — a failing mine cracks across the whole panel. **Amplitude localises** (~9× rise near an event); frequency identifies source type. Not "fixed", because forcing spatial separation would paint in a signal real geophysics does not have. |
| **Soil moisture is asserted, not derived** | See §3.3. Rain and baseline are invented; the precursor link is a modeling choice, not a derivative of the surface. |

---

## 9b. How this data is consumed (Mamba-SSM + spatiotemporal GNN)

The model is **two parts and no more** (spec §1): a Mamba-style State-Space Model
encoding each node's own time series, and a spatiotemporal GNN passing messages
between nodes by spatial layout, producing a per-node per-timestep **hazard
estimate**. There is **no PINN and no physics loss.** Every choice below follows
from that.

### For the SSM (per-node sequences)
- **Uniform 60 s grid, no gaps.** Every node in a mine has the same number of
  timesteps, so a mine stacks into one `(n_nodes, n_steps, n_channels)` tensor
  with no padding or resampling.
- **24 feature channels**, plus `node_id`/`tier`/`t_s`.
- Packet loss is not simulated, which is *why* the grid is gapless. See §9.

### For the GNN (spatial structure)
- `nodes.parquet` gives `(x, y, z)` + tier. **No edge list** — build k-NN or
  radius graphs downstream (spec §6).
- ⚠️ **The Tier 3 gateway is a spatial outlier by design**: it sits 500–1000 m
  outside the angle of draw, so its k-NN distance is ~10× any field node's. A
  naive k-NN graph will attach it to distant nodes and distort message passing.
  **Either exclude the gateway from the graph or give it its own edge rule.**
- Tier is a categorical node feature. Different tiers carry different sensors, so
  the model should embed tier rather than assume homogeneous nodes.

### Structural missingness
Nulls are **not random** — they are constant per tier, because a tier either has
a sensor or does not:

| Tier | Active channels (of 24) |
|---|---|
| 1A | 12 |
| 1B | 14 |
| 1C | 14 |
| 2A | 3 |
| 2B | 6 |
| 3 | 4 |

Treat the null mask as a **fixed property of the tier**, not as missing data to
impute. Imputing it invents sensors that do not exist on that node.

### For the survival head
- Three columns: `time_to_collapse_s`, `censored_flag`, `spatial_weight`.
- `time_to_collapse_s` **decreases monotonically** along each uncensored node's
  sequence, as a time-to-event target must.
- **NaN when censored** — never a sentinel that could pass as a real duration.
- `spatial_weight` is a **separate** column so a trainer can weight the
  likelihood by it or ignore it entirely (spec §5.3).
- A node can be **censored inside a collapsing mine** if no event reached it.
  That is correct: it genuinely survived the horizon.

---

## 10. Train / val / test split

**Split at the whole-mine level, never at node or timestep level** (spec §8).
All nodes and timesteps from a mine go entirely into one split. Splitting
below mine level leaks: nodes in a mine share one underlying stress field, so
a node-level split would produce misleadingly good results.

**Written to `dataset/splits.json`** for the pilot batch. 70 train / 15 val /
15 test whole mines, stratified on `mine_collapses` so the event rate is
balanced (collapsing fraction 0.614 / 0.600 / 0.600 against 0.610 overall).
Split seed `20260905`, deliberately distinct from the per-mine generation
seeds. The three lists are disjoint and cover all 100 mines.

---

## 11. Pilot batch (100 mines) — status and known gate caveats

Generated `2026-09-05` (**regenerated** after the cluster fan-out fix, §2.3/§7.3):
seeds 1–100 into `dataset/`, **100 mines, 5,161 nodes, 58,493,201 rows, 2.04 GB**.

> **Why regenerated.** Anchor counts were previously drawn independently of
> scout counts, yielding up to **13.8 scouts per anchor** — a network that
> cannot physically exist, since an Anchor bundles its children into 138 bytes
> and a Scout packet is 23 bytes (6 max). Anchors are now derived from scouts
> and scouts capped by real anchor capacity, so node counts changed in every
> mine and the previous batch was discarded.

| Quantity | min / median / max |
|---|---|
| nodes per mine | 23 / 51 / 82 |
| horizon (days) | 2.07 / 7.57 / 13.91 |
| rows per mine | 92,287 / 490,416 / 1,522,650 |
| **scouts per anchor (mean)** | **3.2 / 4.8 / 6.0** |
| **max children on any anchor** | **6 — zero breaches across all 100 mines** |
| longest radio link | 1,787 m (60% of the SX1262's 3 km budget) |

61 mines collapse with 121 events total; 39 are fully censored.

**96 of 100 mines pass every gate** (29/29 on collapsing mines, 24/24 on fully
censored ones — the extra five gates only fire when events exist, and now
include the five mesh gates `G11`–`G11e`). The remaining 4 fall one gate short.
Both failure modes are the **same two over-strict gates as the previous batch,
not defective data** — no physics, sensor, noise, label or mesh logic was
changed in response, and **no mesh gate fails in any mine**:

- **G6d "precursor varies per event"** — fails on `mine_00006`, `mine_00013`,
  `mine_00059`. `generate.py` clamps each precursor with
  `min(precursor_days * 86400, 0.7 * horizon_s)`. In a short-horizon mine
  (2.1–3.3 d here) every draw from the 0.3–5.0 d range exceeds the clamp, so
  all events land on the identical clamped value and `nunique() > 1` fails.
  The clamp is correct — a precursor must fit inside the horizon. The gate
  simply does not account for it.
- **G5e "weight not baked into time"** — fails on `mine_00023`, which has a
  single event reaching exactly **one** node. With one node uncensored,
  `spatial_weight` is constant (0.7154), its standard deviation is zero, and
  Pearson correlation is `NaN`; `NaN < 0.999` is False, so the gate fails.
  The columns are genuinely independent — the correlation is undefined, not
  high. A degenerate-input guard would be the fix.

Both are gate-logic issues in `tests/validate.py`, reported rather than
silently patched. Neither affects the usability of the 100-mine batch.
